title: Successor step for bounded abelian henselian comparison
statement: Let (A,I) be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], i:Spec(A/I) → Spec A the quotient-induced map [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and n>0. Fix q≥0. Assume that restriction on H^q [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] is bijective for every abelian etale sheaf F [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] on Spec A killed by n. Then for every such sheaf G restriction on H^(q+1) is bijective.

source.place: Tags 09ZE and 09ZI, finite Z/n coefficient successor step

proof.text: Give G its uniquely determined Z/n-module structure, lifting the finite ring to the coefficient universe. Represent each closed-fibre class by a constructible Z/n-module sheaf C mapping to G. Use constructible filtered colimits, exact inverse image, preservation of colimits by the coefficient forgetful functor, and cohomology continuity. This construction needs no comparison theorem.

Embed C into a finite sum of finite pushforwards of finite constant Z/n-modules (09Z7). Finite exchange and finite-pushforward cohomology identify each closed-fibre component class with a finite constant class on the finite cover. Kill each by 09ZD. Push forward the monic unit of the finite surjective killing cover; the edge/unit compatibility shows that the component class dies. Taking the finite sum and composing with the embedding gives a monomorphism C to C-prime killing the represented class.

Push out C to C-prime along C to G. Pushouts of monomorphisms are monic in the abelian category of Z/n-module sheaves. The pushout identity and functoriality of inverse image and H show that the original class dies. All coefficients remain Z/n-modules, including the cokernel. The same construction for I=0 effaces source classes.

Apply the existing pullbackCohomology_longExact_ladder to the short exact sequences constructed above. For injectivity in degree q+1, take a source class x whose restriction is zero.
   Efface x by a monomorphism G to G', with cokernel Q as above. Exactness gives
   y in H^q(X,Q) with boundary x. On the fibre the boundary of the restriction
   of y is zero, so that restriction comes from z0 in H^q(Z,G'|Z).
   By hprev for G', lift z0 to z in H^q(X,G'). By naturality, the difference
   y minus the image of z restricts to zero. By hprev for Q it is zero. Thus y
   comes from G', so its boundary x is zero.
4. For surjectivity take a fibre class x0 in degree q+1. Efface it by another
   monomorphism G to G' killed by n. Exactness on the fibre gives y0 in
   H^q(Z,Q|Z) with boundary x0. By hprev for Q lift y0 to y in H^q(X,Q).
   Naturality of the boundary maps shows that the boundary of y restricts to x0.
5. Forget the canonical Lambda-module structure. Exact inverse image and exact
   forgetting give the same short exact sequences of abelian sheaves, and the
   compatible cohomology maps are the ones in the statement. For q=0 the
   argument uses only degree-zero comparison and the first boundary. For n=1
   all the coefficient sheaves are zero. For empty spectra the groups are zero.

mathlib_searches.query: Effacement of bounded abelian sheaves implies a successor-degree henselian cohomology comparison from comparison in the preceding degree
A natural map on sheaf cohomology is bijective in successor degree if it is bijective in the preceding degree for all coefficients and positive cohomology classes can be effaced on both sites

theorem bijective_cohomologyMap_succ_of_henselianRing_of_nsmul_eq_zero
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) [HenselianRing A I]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (q : ℕ)
    (hprev : ∀ (F : Sheaf (Spec (.of A)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}),
      n • 𝟙 F = 0 → Function.Bijective
        (cohomologyMap (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) F q))
    (G : Sheaf (Spec (.of A)).smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    (hG : n • 𝟙 G = 0) :
    Function.Bijective
      (cohomologyMap (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) G (q + 1))
